notes: The record of every library piece that STARTED from a CC0 base mesh by elbolilloduro (https://elbolilloduro.itch.io/, models CC0 1.0). blender/tools/build_library.py --extract read these objects ONCE from the local downloads, joined them, resized them to a Japanese size, faced them along the kit convention (the side a person uses faces Blender -Y = Godot +Z) and gave every face a library palette material. None of the downloads' textures were kept. The downloads were then deleted; library.blend owns the pieces.

`fit` scales uniformly so the piece's size along `axis` (x, y, z in Blender after `rot_z`) becomes `size` metres; the sizes are Japanese ones (a shop gondola 1.4 m, a counter 1.0 m, a pump 2.2 m, a vending machine 1.83 m).
`mat` maps a source material name (lower-case substring) to a palette material; the first match wins, then `default`.
`base` is the height of the piece's lowest point above its origin (a wall-mounted basin hangs at 0.72 m).

`fit_box` [w, d, h] (Blender x, y, z after rot_z) re-frames a boxy piece NON-uniformly to a real Japanese size; build_library.py --reframe applies it to the piece already in library.blend (idempotent), because the downloads are gone.

`jp` is the Japan-likeness review: `ok` (reads as Japanese as it is), `reframed` (size fixed here), or `hand` (needs a modeller) with what to change. build_library.py writes it to the collection's `lib_review` property; the README table lists it.

A konbini counter carries a heated hot-snack case (ホットスナック) at the customer end and a cigarette wall behind the clerk; add both. Size (1.0 m high, 0.83 m deep) is right.
Japanese POS: a customer-facing screen, a coin/change machine (自動釣銭機) and an IC-card pad; today it is a plain Western register.
The open chest freezer by the door is typical.
Add the washlet control panel (a small box on the right armrest or a wall remote); the bowl is fine.
Booth seating as at a ファミレス; a call button (呼び出しボタン) on the table would help.

American ground pump. Japanese stations use a slimmer ground unit with a large price panel and hoses on both faces, or, in the city, overhead units hanging from the canopy (懸垂式). Model one of each; the height (2.2 m) is kept.
Make it a JR/Suica gate: a slimmer body (~0.25 m), a lit IC-card pad on the top at the entry end, short flap doors, a direction light; the length 1.3 m is right.
0.8 x 0.55 x 1.8 m (券売機). Still wants a touch screen face and the fare map board above the row.
1.0 x 0.72 x 1.83 m, the Japanese drink machine. Still wants its face: sample bottles behind glass in three rows, a button row, and the take-out slot at the bottom.
Individual plastic seats on a frame, as on Japanese platforms.
Japanese station bins are sorted: a row of three (燃えるゴミ, 缶・びん, ペットボトル) with shaped openings; replace the round Western bin.
A simple shelter reads fine; Japanese ones often have a timetable panel on the side wall.
The Japanese bus stop sign is a round-top plate on a pole with a heavy round concrete base and a timetable box (バス停標識).
